method.h1: One continuous record from two different instruments
method.lead: MODIS (1 km pixels, since 2000) and VIIRS (375 m, since 2012) cannot be compared directly: VIIRS sees about 4.4× more hotspots. Every MODIS day is converted into VIIRS-equivalent hotspots, so 25 years read as one series.
method.step.aggregate.d: 548 M detections into hotspots per 0.5° cell, day and satellite.
method.step.outages.d: A satellite is out when its world count falls under 50% of its 31-day median.
method.step.fit.d: k = VIIRS / MODIS per 1° cell and month, learned 2013–2019.
method.step.validate.d: Scored only on years the factors never saw: 2012 and 2020–2025.
method.step.publish.d: Best source of each day, with its uncertainty.
method.factorText: V and M are VIIRS and MODIS hotspots over 2013–2019. A cell with few hotspots borrows strength from its country, which borrows from the world: world → country → country × month → 1° cell × month. α = 100; each factor stays within ×4 of its parent.
method.src3: MODIS Terra + Aqua, converted; Terra or Aqua alone during an outage.
method.src4: No working satellite: the day is shown as missing, never as zero.
method.outagesAlt: Timeline of satellite outages per satellite
method.validTitle: Median absolute error on unseen years
method.bands: 80% of converted country-months fall within, by size of the predicted count:
method.limitsTitle: What this record cannot tell you
method.limit1: A single day in a small area is not reliable: use months and countries or larger.
method.limit2: MODIS misses small fires, and zero MODIS hotspots cannot be converted.
method.limit3: Terra has drifted since 2020 (about −13% bias when used alone).
method.limit4: 27 days before mid-2002 have no working satellite.
bench.h1: Every method is scored on years it has never seen
bench.lead: Factors are fitted on 2013–2019. Every method is scored on 2012 (first VIIRS year) and 2020–2025. Error = median absolute difference between converted MODIS and observed VIIRS, per month.
bench.footer: Best value per column in bold · lower is better · from manifest.json
data.h1: Download the record and reproduce the analysis
data.lead: Static JSON files with stable schemas, generated {date}. Every harmonized value is keyed by method and version.
data.manifest: Methods (with versions and scores), regions and coverage.
data.series: Monthly series for one region: raw MODIS, raw VIIRS, harmonized per method, days per source.
data.daily: Daily values and the satellite used each day, one file per region and year.
data.cells: 1° grid for one month, harmonized and normal per method.
data.months: Every region for one month, with its normal.
data.uncertainty: Error bands by size of the count, and anomaly agreement.
data.cite: Curious Explorers (2026). Fire Activity: a harmonized MODIS–VIIRS hotspot record, 2000–2025. NASA Space Apps Challenge, CONAE. Source data: NASA FIRMS.
